ds: Inherent-risk factors in how customers are acquired and served. Covers non-face-to-face relationships, intermediaries and introducers, remote onboarding and reliance on third parties.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

cn.rt: Cross-cutting risk factor; applies across all consumer products and channels. Covers remote onboarding and introducers.

rat: Generic channel risk: non-face-to-face onboarding, introducers and third-party reliance.

ind.cx: Customer is onboarded and serviced without any in-person contact.
ind.fp: Digital channels are the norm for many.
ind.ds: Customer is onboarded and serviced without any in-person contact.

ind.cx: Customers originate from agents, brokers or introducers who may not apply adequate checks.
ind.fp: Intermediaries are standard in many industries.
ind.ds: Customers originate from agents, brokers or introducers who may not apply adequate checks.

ind.cx: Institution relies on another entity's due diligence without testing it.
ind.fp: Reliance is permitted when conditions are met.
ind.ds: Institution relies on another entity's due diligence without testing it.

ind.cx: Onboarding relies on a single image or unverified selfie, with no database check.
ind.ds: Onboarding relies on a single image or unverified selfie, with no database check.

ind.n: High volume of onboarding from single source
ind.cx: Unusual surge of accounts via one channel, introducer, IP range or device.
ind.fp: Campaigns and partnerships cause legitimate spikes.
ind.ds: Unusual surge in accounts or claims originating from one channel, introducer, agent, IP range or device.
ind.cn: Spike in volume via a single channel, agent or source

ind.cx: Use of VPN, proxy, anonymising tools or emulators when accessing services.
ind.ds: Use of VPN, proxy, anonymising tools or emulators when accessing services.

ind.n: Agent or branch network with weak oversight
ind.cx: Distributed agents operate with inconsistent controls or limited supervision.
ind.ds: Distributed agents operate with inconsistent controls or limited supervision.

ind.n: Account opened by third party on customer's behalf
ind.cx: Application completed by someone other than the customer without clear authority.
ind.fp: Guardians and professional representatives act lawfully.
ind.ds: Application completed by someone other than the customer without clear authority.

ind.n: Channel used inconsistent with customer profile
ind.cx: Customer uses channels atypical for them, such as a distant branch or sudden switch to digital.
ind.fp: Convenience and travel explain many cases.
ind.ds: Customer uses channels atypical for them, such as a distant branch or sudden switch to digital.

ind.n: Pooled or omnibus access through intermediaries
ind.cx: Intermediaries trade or transact on behalf of undisclosed underlying clients.
ind.fp: Omnibus structures are routine in securities.
ind.ds: Intermediaries trade or transact on behalf of undisclosed underlying clients.

ctl.n: Additional checks for remote and higher-risk onboarding
ctl.ds: Applies supplementary evidence, confirmation calls or direct contact when a customer is onboarded or instructed without meeting in person or presents other higher-risk characteristics. It compensates for the weaker assurance of remote channels.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.

Writes compliance obligations into contracts, including representations, audit rights, termination rights for breach and minimum standards such as wage or disclosure terms. It gives the institution an enforceable lever over counterparties.

Assesses introducers and third parties on whom customer due diligence is relied, covering regulation, data access and file quality, backed by written agreements, per-introducer quality reporting and sample testing. It keeps outsourced onboarding to the institution's own standard.
Monitors business partners after onboarding for adverse media, ownership change, enforcement action and conduct concerns. It keeps third-party risk assessments current between formal reviews.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.

ctl.n: Agent and distribution network due diligence
ctl.ds: Vets, trains, caps and monitors agents, sub-agents and distributors who onboard customers or move funds on the institution's behalf, including quality visits, outlier analysis and disclosure of principals. It limits control failures at the edge of a distribution network.
Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.

Identifies and verifies everyone holding signing, control or power-of-attorney rights over an account, and periodically reviews whether those powers remain justified. It reveals third parties who control accounts on behalf of others.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Secures contractual rights to underlying client information for intermediated or pooled accounts, requires look-through on request and monitors pooled flows against expected activity. It gives visibility of who is really transacting behind an aggregate account.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.
